newsitem.title: ITALY: BASKETBALL-EUROPEAN FINAL FOUR CHAMPIONSHIP PENPIX.
newsitem.headline: BASKETBALL-EUROPEAN FINAL FOUR CHAMPIONSHIP PENPIX.

text.p: Following are penpix of leading players and assessments of main strengths and weaknesses of the four teams in the European Final Four basketball championship starting on Tuesday:
Matches: Olympiakos (Greece) v Ljubljana (Slovenia), Barcelona (Spain) v Villeurbanne (France)
OLYMPIAKOS
Strengths: Famed frontline of Dragan Tarlac and Panayotis Fasoulas. Known as the "twin towers" they are masters of the boards on a good day in scoring, collecting rebounds and blocking.
Weaknesses: Team can be inconsistent; shots from outside the D can be a problem.
Top players:

Dragan Tarlac - A Serb Chicago Bulls hopeful, among the strongest forwards in Europe. Most opponents have trouble guarding him. "Once he gets the ball inside the D the chances are he will score even if two opponents try to stop him. He is a rare talent," FIBA general secretary Borislav Stankovic recently said.
Panayotis Fasoulas - A veteran in European play and Greece's best blocker. Nicknamed the "Spider" he covers the baskets with his long hands and is rarely beaten in one-to-one encounters inside the D.
George Sigalas - Probably Europe's best defender but fouls a lot. On a good day he scores three-pointers and can turn a match around with his explosive style.

David Rivers - The club's fast American playmaker known for his end-to-end runs, perfect assists and shots from outside the D. Can get carried away shooting while he should pass and is lazy in defence.
LJUBLJANA
Strengths: Excellent defence. Well-prepared, physically and mentally.
Weaknesses: Inexperienced at top level. Young team may need another year to be at their best.
Top players:

Vladimir Stepania - Olimpija's tallest centre and member of the Georgian national side is one of the team's best offensive jumpers. However, he lacks experience in big matches and according to coach Zmago Sagadin could work on improving his defensive play as well as his percentage of points scored from close range.

Marko Milic - The first Slovenian player with realistic hopes of joining the NBA after finishing 31st in an NBA draft of young players this year. Considered a very aggressive and fast player. Like most of his team mates, lacks experience in big matches.

Ivica Jurkovic - The man from Bosnia who joined Olimpija only last year is widely regarded as the club's most indispensable defensive player who usually guards the most dangerous opponents. But he appears to lack aggression and physical strength when on the offensive.

Arriel McDonald - The American, who joined Olimpija a year ago, is the team's key organiser and is regarded by his team mates as the personification of calmness. Always highly motivated and fully concentrated, McDonald is famous for keeping his nerve until the end to decide tight matches.
BARCELONA
Strengths: Have improved as the season has gone on thanks largely to the arrival of Serb guard Sasha Djordjevic.
Weaknesses: Over-reliance on occasions on Djordjevic. May be without injured centre Quique Andreu, whose rebound expertise will be especially missed.
Top players:

Aleksandar ('Sasha') Djordjevic - Joined the side from Teamsystem Bologna in January after Russian forward Andrei Fetissov failed to come up with the goods and has revolutionised Barcelona's play. Strong in assists and a fine triple-shot man.

Arturas Karnishovas - Along with Djordjevic the Lithuanian is the major figure in the team and is also good from the triple shot line. Often fragile at key moments and failed to live up to expectations in last year's dramatic European defeat by Panathinaikos.

Andres Jimenez - The veteran captain has been present in all five Final Fours played by Barcelona since 1987. Power forward, has regained importance in the team because of injury problems in the centre position. Strong close to the hoop.

Roberto Duenas - Shaking off the image of uncoordinated giant with recent performances in which he has successfully disrupted the shooting strategies of opponents. A good rebound man. Duenas's recently-renewed contract prevents him going to any team except those in the NBA -- where he is already arousing interest.
VILLEURBANNE
Strengths: Good in a tight finish with 7-0 record in the qualifying pools in matches that finished with less than five points difference. Play well as a team and tactically astute.
Weakness: Will badly miss the injured Jim Bilba in defence.
Leading players::
Alain Digbeu - Has developed into one of the most spectacular players in Europe with a good three-point record. Could make the NBA this summer.
Delaney Rudd - Fine passer with good shooting sense. Selected for first EuroStars match and voted foreign MVP in French top division for last seasons.

Brian Howard - Complete player with very accurate shot who joined from Dallas. Is coming back from ankle injury which put him out of action for final two months of last year. Coach Beugnot calls him "Silent assassin".

Ronnie Smith - Victim of serious knee injury at start of season, Smith has just returned to full competition and should help, if he recovers enough of his mobility, to make up in defence for loss through injury of Jim Bilba. American-born naturalised Frenchman who has been voted French MVP.
